entries.note: take 3's face tracking is kept; the 36 widest yawn frames its outlier test had thrown out are put back
the first tracked turn (62°) gives the axis the chair spins about
no face to track from behind, so the turn is read from how the hair moves frame to frame, separating turn from slide
when both ears show equal skin either side of the hair, he is seen from exactly behind: six such instants pin the turn
outline agreement is flat across flow scales (0.763 to 0.776), so the ears, not the outline, set the scale
each frame's person mask snapped to image edges with a guided filter
the head carved on a 2 mm grid; back views would trim only 1% more, so they are left out
the carve is streaky on the scalp from pose noise: smoothed harder there than on the ears and nose
±70° of tracked turn leaves a ridge of at most 6 mm down the back: rounded off
shoulders are not rigid with the head, so only the neck column is kept below the jaw
tracked face and carve disagree by -6 to +11 mm at the rim; the face is shifted to meet the carve there
inside the face the tracked points cut what an outline cannot see: eye sockets, lips, nose wings
15 frame pairs 14° apart, two independent sets: their relief maps agree at r = 0.39. Too noisy: not used
the carve's own neck runs into a bust block with trapezius slopes
nostrils at the tracked points; a concha hollow where the carve put each ear
vermilion edge along the 20-point lip line
hair raised 1.6 mm with stipple where the frames, and the paint's own darkness, say hair
collar band and fabric layer; two tooth arches; 2.4 cm eyeballs behind the lids
slow, calm frames only: one frontal, four sides, below, above, six from behind
the surface is given that frame's expression, then the frame is projected on, hidden texels skipped
each new view is colour-matched to what is painted, then nudged into register by optical flow (6 to 10 texels)
broad colour blended widely, fine detail taken from the single best view, so it stays sharp
going round the head both ways leaves two exposures meeting at the back: cross-faded, hair tone evened
irises and whites sampled from the frontal frame through its own eyelid outline
a full turn of the painted bust
43,462 vertices follow the tracked points through the face map
PCA of the tracked face motion keeps 97.3%
each frame's head rotation = a turn about the chair axis (up to ±200°) + what the neck did (up to 48°)
the sculpt performs the clip, spins included; the page plays all 47 seconds live
